model.title: Emergency Conservation Program Improvement Act of 2025

summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Public Law):

blocks.text: Emergency Conservation Program Improvement Act of 2025

This act revises the Emergency Conservation Program (ECP) and the Emergency Forest Restoration Program (EFRP) to expand eligibility for payments to agricultural producers and owners of forest land impacted by natural disasters. The act also provides additional options to receive an advance on cost-sharing payments before carrying out emergency measures.

The act expands advance ECP payments to include the replacement, repair, or restoration of farmland or conservation structures requiring an immediate response. Producers may receive an advance on cost-sharing payments for 75% of the cost of the replacement and 50% of the cost of the repair or restoration. Current law limits advance payments to 25% of the cost of the repair or replacement of fencing.

Under EFRP, the act allows owners of nonindustrial private forest land impacted by a natural disaster to receive an advance on cost-sharing payments for up to 75% of the cost of the emergency measures. Currently, advance payments are not available under the program.
ECP and EFRP recipients must use the funds within 180 days after the funds are disbursed. This provides additional time to ECP recipients who currently must use the funds within 60 days.

The act also expands eligibility for payments under the programs to include emergency measures to address damages caused by (1) a wildfire that is not caused naturally, if the damage is caused by the spread of the wildfire due to natural causes; and (2) a wildfire that is caused by the federal government.

This act changes two federal disaster programs that help farmers and private forest owners recover from natural disasters: the Emergency Conservation Program (ECP) and the Emergency Forest Restoration Program (EFRP). It makes more people eligible for payments and lets them get money sooner.

Under the ECP, the act allows advance payments for replacing, repairing, or restoring farmland or conservation structures that need immediate attention. Producers could receive an advance of 75% of the cost of a replacement and 50% of the cost of a repair or restoration. Right now, advance payments are limited to 25% of the cost of repairing or replacing fencing.

For the EFRP, owners of private forest land that is not used for industrial purposes could receive an advance of up to 75% of the cost of emergency measures after a natural disaster. Advance payments are not currently available under this program.
Recipients of ECP and EFRP funds would have 180 days after the money is paid out to use it. ECP recipients currently have only 60 days.

The act also widens eligibility for both programs. Emergency measures would now cover damage from a wildfire that was not caused by natural causes, if natural causes such as wind or weather then spread it. It would also cover damage from a wildfire caused by the federal government.
